key_insight: AMIFound is a single foundation model that can restore and enhance medical images across seven different imaging modalities. It improves image quality while preserving clinically important details needed for diagnosis.
problem_solved: Medical images often suffer from modality-specific degradations such as noise, blur, low contrast, and artifacts, and current restoration methods are typically built for one modality at a time. This creates fragmented tools and inconsistent performance across diverse clinical imaging data.
method: Trains a unified foundation model, AMIFound, to handle restoration and enhancement across multiple medical imaging modalities.
Learns from diverse degradation patterns so one model can generalize to different image types and quality issues.
Prioritizes both visual enhancement and preservation of diagnostic content, avoiding over-smoothing or loss of clinically relevant structures.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows that a general-purpose medical image restoration model can reduce the need for separate modality-specific systems. It also highlights a practical path toward more scalable and clinically useful imaging AI.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing seven imaging modalities feeding into one foundation model and outputting restored images
Before-and-after image panels illustrating denoising, deblurring, and contrast enhancement
An icon grid representing the different degradations handled by the model
A comparison chart showing unified model performance versus separate modality-specific baselines
paper_title: An all-in-one foundation model for multimodal medical image restoration and enhancement
paper_authors: Luyang Cao, Zhijian Wu, Jian Zhang, Lei Qi, Yang Gao
